title: Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy Bill 2021
short_title: Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would impose industry levies to finance the financial services compensation scheme of last resort, covering compensation, unpaid complaint fees, administration and reserves.
Annual and additional levies would fund relevant industry sub-sectors, with a $250 million overall cap per levy period and a normally $10 million sub-sector cap.
A one-off levy would cover accumulated eligible claims, while the Commonwealth would fund establishment and first-year operations under the companion legislation's broader scheme.
changes: Regulations would prescribe which industry sub-sectors paid annual levies and how individual firms' liabilities were calculated.
Further levies could meet revised funding estimates within the relevant sub-sector cap.
Special levies could exceed a sub-sector cap following a ministerial determination, while remaining within the overall scheme cap.
The one-off levy would fall on specified large banking and insurance entities, excluding private health insurers and superannuation trustees.
summary.affected: Financial firms in prescribed sub-sectors and specified large financial groups would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The Financial Services Compensation Scheme of Last Resort Levy Bill 2021 was moved for second reading, establishing a levy framework funded by industry entities through an annual levy starting January 2023, with sub-sector caps of $10 million and an overall cap of $250 million, plus a one-off levy on the ten largest financial sector entities in 2022-23 and provision for special levies in response to unforeseen events.
